_comment: The registry of every declared difference between `jaune t8n` and the conformance target on the committed corpus. scripts/check-t8n.sh applies each entry to the GOLDEN side before comparing; nothing is applied to Jaune's output, whose bytes are compared as written. Each entry pins Jaune's exact expected bytes as well as the target's, so an unregistered difference and a changed registered one both fail the gate. scripts/report-t8n.md carries the full justification.
_messages_comment: `rejected[].error` and `blockException` carry free text with no normative content. Every transition tool writes its own, and the framework maps the text to a canonical identity through the registered wrapper's exception mapper rather than comparing it (execution_testing/exceptions/exception_mapper.py). Jaune therefore writes its own canonical vocabulary -- the official identity Jaune/FixtureException.lean already assigns to each typed reason -- rather than imitating another tool's wording. Every pair below maps to the same official identity on both sides.
_fields_comment: Per-case field exemptions. Each names the document, the JSON path, the target's exact value, Jaune's exact value, and why they differ. An entry whose target-side mechanism has been reported upstream also carries an `upstream` line naming the filing; scripts ignore the key.

fields.why: The case's first transaction is a type-3 blob transaction with no receiver -- a shape every fork on this lane rejects, and one Jaune's `TxType.three` cannot represent at all because its receiver is a mandatory `Adr`. The target builds the object anyway and rejects it one step later, inside `check_transaction`; because `process_transaction` writes into the shared `block_output.transactions_trie` before validating, the unexecutable transaction is still counted by `txRoot` and is still encoded into `body`. Jaune classifies the same shape at decode, with the same official identity (TransactionException.TYPE_3_TX_CONTRACT_CREATION), so `rejected` agrees; it simply has no transaction object to put in the trie or the body. The framework consumes neither field -- specs/blockchain.py excludes `transactions_trie` from the fixture header and recomputes it, and the body is not read back -- and widening the type to represent an invalid shape would weaken Jaune, not the tool.
fields.upstream: The target-side mechanism -- the pre-validation write into the shared transactions trie -- was filed upstream 2026-08-11 as ethereum/execution-specs#3362 (https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/issues/3362). Target defect, not a Jaune bug; the entry stands until the anchor is re-pinned past a fix.
